title_fa: جوزف فینک، خالق Night Vale خوش آمدید، داستان سرایی را از گریم فاندانگو آموخت
excerpt_en: Joseph Fink is the cocreator and cowriter of Welcome to Night Vale, arguably the most important fiction podcast ever. He's also the creator of the noir podcast Unlicensed and Alice Isn't Dead, which takes some of the conspiratorial cosmic horror of Night Vale and turns it into...
excerpt_fa: جوزف فینک یکی از خالقان و نویسنده‌های خوش آمدید به Night Vale است، که مسلما مهم‌ترین پادکست داستانی تا کنون است. او همچنین خالق پادکست نوآر Unlicensed و Alice Isn't Dead است که بخشی از وحشت توطئه آمیز کیهانی Night Vale را می گیرد و آن را به ...
content_en:
Joseph Fink is the cocreator and cowriter of Welcome to Night Vale, arguably the most important fiction podcast ever. He’s also the creator of the noir podcast Unlicensed and Alice Isn’t Dead, which takes some of the conspiratorial cosmic horror of Night Vale and turns it into fodder for a more serious series about relationships, trauma, and the open road. There’s also a sequel series out now called Don’t Tell Alice that takes the story down an even darker path in which protagonist Keisha is the one with a secret.
Welcome to Night Vale cocreator Joseph Fink learned storytelling from Grim Fandango
His latest book, The Nudge, tells the tale of a man who can’t seem to outrun a mysterious evil.
Welcome to Night Vale cocreator Joseph Fink learned storytelling from Grim Fandango
His latest book, The Nudge, tells the tale of a man who can’t seem to outrun a mysterious evil.
Joseph is also an accomplished author. In addition to co-writing the three Welcome to Night Vale novels, he’s also penned the Alice Isn’t Dead novel and The Halloween Moon. His latest work is The Nudge, which features some gorgeous illustrations from Jessica Hayworth, who also provides the art for Night Vale, hits shelves on September 1st. It’s a brief and unsettling novella about a man trying to outrun some mysterious evil.
What is the first app you install on a new phone or computer?
Podcast Addict. It’s an Android-only podcast app made by one guy named Xavier, and it is so much better than any other podcast app that it’s the main reason I can never switch to an iPhone. I’m maybe the one guy in the entire country who chooses phones based on how they play podcasts.
Which social media platform do you use the most?
I use Bluesky, which I used to like because no one was there and so no one read my posts, which is really the ideal social media for me. Now there are more people there, and sometimes people read and respond to my posts, which is a drag.
What game do you have the fondest memories of?
My entire understanding of storytelling is probably shaped by Grim Fandango, a 1999 adventure game about a sad sack grim reaper navigating a film noir afterlife. There are lines and images from that game that will live in my head forever, even if a lot of them were parodies or references to classic films I wasn’t even aware existed when I first played that game.
What creation are you most proud of?
Our Audible show Unlicensed was one of those few projects that turned out exactly how I wanted it to in my head. A mystery series set in the least cool parts of Los Angeles, the parts where the actual people live. I didn’t want it to be “good for two writers who usually don’t write mysteries.” I just wanted us to write a damn good mystery, and I think we did. We got three seasons out of Audible, but then they mostly shut down their original shows department, and that was it. If I had my choice though, I’d happily spend the rest of my life writing Unlicensed.
What’s the best piece of advice you’ve ever received?
I recently watched a talk with Meshell Ndegeocello, and she described having to shush a fellow student in a guitar workshop who was noodling on his guitar while the teacher was trying to demonstrate something. Meshell said: “As a musician, it doesn’t matter how well you play if you can’t listen.” I don’t know if it’s the best advice I’ve ever received, but I think it’s damn good advice and applies to a lot of things outside of music.
What’s the last piece of physical media you bought?
I buy too many books, constantly. I like to hang out in bookstores, and I’ve never left one without buying at least a couple of books. I’m mostly not a physical media guy, I have no interest in owning records or DVDs, but I’ll build an addition to my house before I get rid of any books.
What would the tagline for your biopic be?
“It turns out watching a guy write audio fiction on his computer is boring, this movie was a mistake sorry, we’re sorry.”
What’s the last GIF or meme you used?
I don’t really use GIFs or memes. I’m very much a text guy, which is why I stick to text social media mostly, even though that doesn’t really help you sell books or stuff like that.

معتاد به پادکست. این یک برنامه پادکست فقط برای اندروید است که توسط شخصی به نام Xavier ساخته شده است و آنقدر بهتر از هر برنامه پادکست دیگری است که دلیل اصلی من هرگز نمی توانم به آیفون تغییر دهم. شاید من تنها مردی در کل کشور باشم که گوشی ها را بر اساس نحوه پخش پادکست انتخاب می کنم.
از کدام شبکه اجتماعی بیشتر استفاده می کنید؟
من از Bluesky استفاده می کنم که قبلاً آن را دوست داشتم زیرا هیچ کس آنجا نبود و بنابراین هیچ کس پست های من را نمی خواند که واقعاً رسانه اجتماعی ایده آل برای من است. اکنون افراد بیشتری در آنجا هستند و گاهی اوقات مردم پست های من را می خوانند و به آنها پاسخ می دهند که این یک کشش است.
بهترین خاطره از کدام بازی دارید؟
کل درک من از داستان سرایی احتمالاً توسط گریم فاندانگو شکل گرفته است، یک بازی ماجراجویی در سال 1999 درباره یک دروگر غمگین کیسه ای که در حال گشت و گذار در زندگی پس از مرگ فیلم نوآر است. خطوط و تصاویری از آن بازی وجود دارد که برای همیشه در ذهن من باقی می‌ماند، حتی اگر بسیاری از آنها تقلید یا ارجاع به فیلم‌های کلاسیک باشند، من حتی از وجود آن‌ها در اولین بازی خود اطلاعی نداشتم.
به کدام خلقت بیشتر افتخار می کنید؟
نمایش شنیدنی ما بدون مجوز یکی از معدود پروژه‌هایی بود که دقیقاً همان طور که می‌خواستم در ذهنم ظاهر شد. سریالی رازآلود که در کم‌نظیرترین بخش‌های لس‌آنجلس اتفاق می‌افتد، قسمت‌هایی که مردم واقعی در آن زندگی می‌کنند. نمی‌خواستم «برای دو نویسنده‌ای که معمولاً اسرار نمی‌نویسند خوب باشد». من فقط می خواستم یک معمای لعنتی خوب بنویسیم و فکر می کنم این کار را کردیم. ما سه فصل از Audible را پخش کردیم، اما سپس آنها عمدتاً بخش نمایش اصلی خود را تعطیل کردند و تمام. اگر انتخابم را داشتم، با خوشحالی بقیه عمرم را صرف نوشتن بدون مجوز می‌کردم.
بهترین توصیه ای که تا به حال دریافت کرده اید چیست؟
من اخیراً صحبتی را با مشل ندژئوچلو تماشا کردم، و او توضیح داد که باید یکی از دانش‌آموزان را در یک کارگاه گیتار که مشغول نودل زدن با گیتار خود بود، در حالی که معلم سعی می‌کرد چیزی را نشان دهد، خفه کند. مشل گفت: "به عنوان یک نوازنده، مهم نیست که چقدر خوب می نوازی اگر نتوانی گوش کنی." نمی‌دانم این بهترین توصیه‌ای است که تا به حال دریافت کرده‌ام یا نه، اما فکر می‌کنم این توصیه خوبی است و برای بسیاری از چیزهای خارج از موسیقی کاربرد دارد.
آخرین قطعه رسانه فیزیکی که خریدید چیست؟
من دائماً کتاب های زیادی می خرم. من دوست دارم در کتابفروشی ها بنشینم و هرگز یکی را بدون خرید حداقل چند کتاب ترک نکرده ام. من اکثراً اهل رسانه فیزیکی نیستم، علاقه‌ای به داشتن صفحه یا دی‌وی‌دی ندارم، اما قبل از اینکه از شر هر کتابی خلاص شوم، اضافاتی به خانه‌ام خواهم ساخت.
شعار فیلم بیوگرافی شما چه خواهد بود؟
"معلوم شد که تماشای یک مرد در حال نوشتن داستان های صوتی در رایانه خود خسته کننده است، این فیلم یک اشتباه بود متأسفیم، ما متاسفیم."
آخرین GIF یا میمی که استفاده کردید چیست؟
من واقعاً از GIF یا میم استفاده نمی کنم. من بسیار یک پسر پیام رسان هستم، به همین دلیل است که بیشتر به شبکه های اجتماعی پیامک می پردازم، حتی اگر واقعاً به شما در فروش کتاب یا چیزهای مشابه کمک نمی کند.

title_en: OpenAI will pull its models from Cursor due to SpaceXAI acquisition
title_fa: OpenAI will pull its models from Cursor due to SpaceXAI acquisition
excerpt_en: OpenAI is planning to cut off Cursor's access to its models on November 12, 2026.
excerpt_fa: OpenAI is planning to cut off Cursor's access to its models on November 12, 2026.
content_en:
OpenAI will pull its models from Cursor due to SpaceXAI acquisition
The company said it’s not confident that SpaceXAI will follow its terms of service based on its experience with Elon Musk.
OpenAI is planning to cut off Cursor's access from its models, following the AI coding assistant's acquisition by SpaceXAI. In a post on its website, the company said it's giving Cursor users as much time as it could based on its contract. It intends to pull its models from the service on November 12, 2026, but it said that Cursor could choose an earlier termination date.
The company explained that it's making this choice because it can't be confident that SpaceX will use its technology within its terms of services, based on its "experience with Elon Musk's companies violating contracts." OpenAI and Musk have a long and troubled history, with the SpaceXAI chief being one of the company's earliest investors. He allegedly left in 2018 when OpenAI refused to implement a new board structure he proposed that would give him control of the company.
In 2024, Musk filed a lawsuit to stop OpenAI from transitioning into a for-profit company from a nonprofit organization. He accused OpenAI of violating its founding mission of building AI "for the benefit of humanity" and of telling investors not to fund rival AI firms like xAI. Just this May, a jury ruled against Musk, and the judge in the case dismissed his claims of "breach of charitable trust and unjust enrichment."
In its post, OpenAI specifically pointed to what Musk admitted during a cross-examination for that lawsuit as one example of how he and xAI had violated its terms of service. Musk admitted that xAI used Open AI's output to train its own models in a process called distillation. OpenAI also previously accused Chinese startups, including DeepSeek, of "distilling" its models.
"As AI capabilities advance, we also have a new level of accountability to ensure our upcoming model, Astra, is being used in accordance with our terms," OpenAI wrote. "Given all of this, we've decided to hold the contract cancellation to the latest date we can while not providing future models to Cursor." The company recently slowed down Astra's development due to cybersecurity concerns after its AI agents escaped their supposed isolated testing environments and broke into AI platform Hugging Face.
Cursor co-founder and CEO Michael Truell said in a post on X that OpenAI serves five percent of the tool's customers. He revealed that his team is speaking with the company's in hopes of coming up with a resolution. Meanwhile, Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown said his company will "continue to increase compute to support Claude models in Cursor" and that it's "excited for what comes next with them at SpaceX."

title_en: Why clearing cache won't always speed up your devices
title_fa: Why clearing cache won't always speed up your devices
excerpt_en: Clearing cache is a handy troubleshooting step, but you shouldn't use it all the time. Reckless use can actually slow your apps and devices down for a while.
excerpt_fa: Clearing cache is a handy troubleshooting step, but you shouldn't use it all the time. Reckless use can actually slow your apps and devices down for a while.
content_en:
Why clearing cache won't always speed up your devices
Cached files are meant to reduce repeat work, so clearing them can actually be counter-productive.
Clearing cached data has become a catch-all troubleshooting tip people recommend whenever a phone, computer or streaming device feels slow. While this can help sometimes, cached data isn't inherently bad for performance. A cache exists so software can reuse information instead of downloading or rebuilding it every time.
If that stored data is causing a problem or taking up storage you need elsewhere, clearing it can help. If not, you're deleting information the program may immediately have to fetch or recreate, which is a waste of time.
Your cache is supposed to save your device work
A cache is temporary storage for information that software expects to use again. In a browser, that can include copies of images and other parts of a webpage. Rather than downloading the same resources every time you return, the browser will reuse what it already stored, which makes repeat visits faster.
Apps use the same basic idea, although what they cache varies. A music streaming app might cache playlists you listen to frequently so they're ready to go immediately, while a social media app may cache thumbnails and profile pictures from pages you're visited recently. Holding this temporary information saves them from fetching or recreating it every time you open the app.
A large cache isn't automatically evidence that something is wrong. In many cases, that stored data is doing exactly what it was designed to do. There also isn't one universal cache shared across your device. A browser cache, an individual app's cache and system-level caches can serve different purposes and are cleared in different ways. Treating all of them as disposable clutter misses why they exist in the first place.
Clearing cache can slow performance down before it helps
Deleting cached data removes the "shortcut" it provides. Apps and the operating system can build the cache again, but they first have to retrieve or recreate what you removed.
Google makes that trade-off explicit in its guidance for clearing Chrome's cache and cookies. Some websites can seem slower after clearing cache since heavy content, such as images, has to load again. For Android, Google gives a similar warning: some apps may be slower the next time you open them after clearing their cache.
That doesn't mean clearing a cache is useless. If the stored data itself is contributing to a loading problem, forcing the software to replace it can help. For instance, if a cached video becomes corrupted, it won't load properly when you open it.
Clearing cached data can also free storage, but that's a separate benefit from making apps faster. If cached data isn't causing the slowdown, deleting it doesn't resolve the underlying problem. Additionally, any space gained from clearing cache is short-lived, since it will be recreated before long.
Clear cache only when cached data is the problem
Cache clearing makes the most sense as targeted troubleshooting, not routine maintenance. Google lists website loading or formatting problems among the reasons to clear browser cache and cookies. If an Android app is misbehaving and provides a dedicated cache control, clearing that app's temporary data can serve a similar purpose without touching unrelated apps.
Some devices also provide cache-clearing tools for specific system problems. For example, you can clear the system software cache on your PS5 using safe mode, which Sony recommends for system feature issues or performance drops. The distinction is how Sony points to a specific system cache as a troubleshooting step, rather than recommending routine cache clearing as a general cleanup step.
This is why the blanket instruction to "clear your cache" isn't particularly useful on its own. You first need to know what's going wrong and which cache could plausibly be involved. If an app, browser or device is working normally and storage isn't a concern, there's little reason to clear caches on a schedule.
Cache, cookies and app data are not the same
The phrase "clear the cache" gets even less precise when the cleanup menu offers several categories of stored data.
Chrome, for example, treats cached images and files separately from cookies, browsing history and other site information. Cookies can preserve sign-ins and site preferences, while cached files are primarily reusable page resources. Clearing cookies will thus have a bigger effect on how websites remember you than clearing cached files alone.
Android makes the distinction especially clear. Google's app storage controls separate Clear cache (which deletes temporary data) from Clear storage, which permanently deletes all app data. Those are distinct actions, even though the buttons appear close together in Settings.
Safari uses a different setup. When clearing the cache on your iPhone, Clear History and Website Data removes history, cache and cookies together, while website data can also be removed separately if you want to keep your browsing history.
Before you tap Delete or Clear, check which categories are selected. Cached files are temporary. Cookies, browsing history and app data can contain information you may want to keep, and deleting the wrong category can do considerably more than clearing a cache.

title_en: The Theragun Sense makes everyday recovery surprisingly easy
title_fa: Theragun Sense بهبودی روزمره را به طرز شگفت آوری آسان می کند
excerpt_en: As my 20s are set to come to an end later this year, I’ve officially reached the age where sleeping in the wrong position or stretching just a little too far can cause aches and pains. I’ve always been somewhat skeptical of massage guns, mostly because I’ve tried a few off-brand...
excerpt_fa: از آنجایی که قرار است اواخر امسال 20 سالگی من به پایان برسد، من رسماً به سنی رسیده ام که خوابیدن در وضعیت نامناسب یا کشش کمی بیش از حد می تواند باعث درد و درد شود. من همیشه تا حدودی به تفنگ های ماساژ بدبین بوده ام، بیشتر به این دلیل که چند مدل غیر مارک را امتحان کرده ام...
content_en:
As my 20s are set to come to an end later this year, I’ve officially reached the age where sleeping in the wrong position or stretching just a little too far can cause aches and pains. I’ve always been somewhat skeptical of massage guns, mostly because I’ve tried a few off-brand ones and just assumed they’d eventually end up collecting dust in a drawer.
But after a few weeks of testing the Therabody Theragun Sense (2nd Gen), I was surprised. Turns out massage guns aren’t as gimmicky as I had thought.
The Theragun Sense, which retails for $299, is a wellness-focused massage gun that’s designed for everyday aches, muscle tension, relaxation, and soreness. It’s more of a gentle massaging and relaxation tool rather than a hardcore recovery massage gun.
If you’re looking for more of a deep-tissue massage, it might be worth checking out the Theragun PRO or Prime. But if you don’t need a super heavy-duty massage gun with features like heated therapy and deep- tissue capabilities, the Theragun Sense is a great option for everyday use.
My favorite thing about the massage gun is that it features built-in visually guided routines. The device comes with four routines, and you can access additional routines through the Therabody app and sync your favorite ones to the device using Bluetooth.
The Theragun Sense has an LCD screen that walks you through routines step by step. Once you select a routine, the screen shows you exactly where to use the massage gun, how long to spend on each area, and how much pressure to apply.
As someone who never really had an idea of what to do with a massage gun other than pointing it to a sore muscle and hoping for the best, I liked that the Therabody Sense takes a lot of the guesswork out of using a massage gun.
My favorite routine was the six-minute “Sleep” routine that’s essentially a quick full-body massage to get you ready for the night. The app lets you choose from many other routines, like “Pre-Walk Warm-up,” “Desk Relief,” “Lower Back Recovery,” and more.
The massage gun features five speeds to fine-tune pressure to allow for a more relaxing touch, moderate pressure, or a deeper tension release. I liked having the flexibility to change the intensity depending on how sore I was feeling that day.
Since the device is designed to be lightweight, I found it easy to hold and get to those spots on my back and shoulders that are harder to reach.
For people who want more personalization, the Therabody app takes the guided experience a step further with Coach, the company’s AI feature that creates personalized recovery recommendations based on your goals and activity. Coach can recommend which part of your body to target, which settings or attachments to use, and when to fit a recovery session into your day.
The relatively quiet motor was another feature I appreciated, as I could easily use the device while watching TV or relaxing without the sound of the massage gun acting as a distraction.
The Theragun Sense comes with a USB-C charging cable, a travel pouch, and two massage attachments: the Standard Ball and the Dampener, which is designed to target knots and tender areas. Separately, you can purchase the “Supersoft” attachment for $35 for extra sensitive areas on the body.
Overall, the Theragun Sense (2nd Gen) won me over. It’s easy to use, comfortable to hold, and notably takes the guesswork out of using a massage gun. At $299, it isn’t cheap, but I think it’s a great option for people who want an everyday wellness device that can help them relax and recover.

از آنجایی که قرار است اواخر امسال 20 سالگی من به پایان برسد، من رسماً به سنی رسیده ام که خوابیدن در وضعیت نامناسب یا کشش کمی بیش از حد می تواند باعث درد و درد شود. من همیشه تا حدودی نسبت به تفنگ های ماساژ بدبین بوده ام، بیشتر به این دلیل که چند اسلحه غیر مارک را امتحان کرده ام و فقط تصور می کنم که در نهایت گرد و غبار را در کشو جمع می کنند.

Theragun Sense که با قیمت 299 دلار به فروش می رسد، یک تفنگ ماساژ متمرکز بر سلامتی است که برای دردهای روزمره، تنش عضلانی، آرامش و درد طراحی شده است. این بیشتر یک ابزار ماساژ ملایم و آرامش بخش است تا یک تفنگ ماساژ ریکاوری هاردکور.
اگر به دنبال ماساژ عمیق تر هستید، ممکن است ارزش بررسی Theragun PRO یا Prime را داشته باشد. اما اگر به یک تفنگ ماساژ بسیار سنگین با ویژگی‌هایی مانند گرمایش درمانی و قابلیت‌های بافت عمیق نیاز ندارید، Theragun Sense یک گزینه عالی برای استفاده روزمره است.
چیز مورد علاقه من در مورد تفنگ ماساژ این است که دارای روال های هدایت بصری داخلی است. این دستگاه دارای چهار روال است و می توانید از طریق برنامه Therabody به روال های اضافی دسترسی داشته باشید و موارد دلخواه خود را با استفاده از بلوتوث با دستگاه همگام کنید.
Theragun Sense دارای یک صفحه نمایش LCD است که شما را به صورت گام به گام در کارهای روزمره راهنمایی می کند. هنگامی که یک روال را انتخاب می کنید، صفحه نمایش دقیقاً به شما نشان می دهد که کجا از تفنگ ماساژ استفاده کنید، چه مدت برای هر ناحیه صرف کنید، و چه مقدار فشار باید اعمال کنید.
به‌عنوان کسی که هیچ‌وقت نمی‌دانستم با تفنگ ماساژور چه کار کنم، به جز اشاره کردن به عضله دردناک و امید به بهترین‌ها، دوست داشتم که Therabody Sense از حدس و گمان استفاده از تفنگ ماساژ استفاده کند.
روال مورد علاقه من روال شش دقیقه ای "خواب" بود که اساساً یک ماساژ سریع کل بدن است تا شما را برای شب آماده کند. این برنامه به شما امکان می‌دهد از بین بسیاری از برنامه‌های روتین دیگر مانند «گرم کردن قبل از پیاده‌روی»، «تسکین میز»، «بازیابی کمر» و موارد دیگر انتخاب کنید.
تفنگ ماساژ دارای پنج سرعت برای تنظیم دقیق فشار است تا امکان لمس آرامش‌بخش‌تر، فشار متوسط ​​یا آزاد شدن تنش عمیق‌تر را فراهم کند. من دوست داشتم این انعطاف پذیری را داشته باشم تا بسته به میزان درد آن روز، شدت آن را تغییر دهم.
از آنجایی که دستگاه به گونه‌ای طراحی شده است که سبک وزن باشد، به راحتی می‌توانم آن نقاطی را در پشت و شانه‌هایم که دسترسی به آن‌ها سخت‌تر است، در دست بگیرم و برسم.
برای افرادی که خواهان شخصی‌سازی بیشتر هستند، اپلیکیشن Therabody با Coach، ویژگی هوش مصنوعی این شرکت که توصیه‌های بازیابی شخصی‌شده را بر اساس اهداف و فعالیت‌های شما ایجاد می‌کند، تجربه هدایت‌شده را یک قدم جلوتر می‌برد. مربی می‌تواند توصیه کند که کدام قسمت از بدن شما را هدف قرار دهید، از کدام تنظیمات یا پیوست‌ها استفاده کنید، و چه زمانی یک جلسه ریکاوری را در روز خود جای دهید.
موتور نسبتا بی صدا یکی دیگر از ویژگی هایی بود که من از آن استقبال می کردم، زیرا می توانستم به راحتی از دستگاه در حین تماشای تلویزیون یا استراحت استفاده کنم بدون اینکه صدای تفنگ ماساژ باعث حواس پرتی شود.
Theragun Sense دارای یک کابل شارژ USB-C، یک کیسه مسافرتی و دو ضمیمه ماساژ است: توپ استاندارد و دمپنر، که برای هدف قرار دادن گره ها و نواحی حساس طراحی شده است. به طور جداگانه، می توانید پیوست "Supersoft" را با قیمت 35 دلار برای نواحی حساس اضافی بدن خریداری کنید.
به طور کلی، Theragun Sense (نسل دوم) من را برنده شد. استفاده از آن آسان است، در دست گرفتن راحت است، و به ویژه حدس و گمان استفاده از تفنگ ماساژ را از بین می برد. با قیمت 299 دلار، ارزان نیست، اما فکر می‌کنم برای افرادی که می‌خواهند یک دستگاه سلامتی روزانه داشته باشند که بتواند به آنها آرامش و بهبودی کمک کند، گزینه‌ای عالی است.

title_en: Engadget review recap: Google's Pixel 11 series and more
title_fa: خلاصه بررسی Engadget: سری پیکسل 11 گوگل و موارد دیگر
excerpt_en: A roundup of recent reviews from Engadget.
excerpt_fa: A roundup of recent reviews from Engadget.
content_en:
Engadget review recap: Google's Pixel 11 series and more
A roundup of recent reviews from Engadget.
With IFA just around the corner (literally next week), we're coming off another deluge of devices for our reviews team. There's plenty to catch up on, including a quartet of Google's latest Pixel wares. Read on for more than just phones and a watch, as we've done plenty of other gadget testing for your weekend reading.
Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold
Google introduced several upgrades on the Pixel 11 Pro Fold, but it opted not to change the series' chunky design. The company also decided not to give its flagship foldable all of the features from the regular Pixel 11 Pro, like Pro Res Zoom. "The big issue for the Pixel 11 Pro Fold is that while a new chip, faster charging and an upgraded camera are all nice additions, I don't think Google has done enough to entice shoppers that aren't already entrenched in the Pixel ecosystem," senior reviews writer Sam Rutherford said.
Google Pixel 11 Pro
The Pixel 11 Pro may be the most powerful and feature-packed option in Google's new lineup, but the phone is $100 more and has less RAM than before. There's also a lot of AI baked in. "I have deep misgivings about the pervasiveness of AI features here, but I can't deny that at the moment, Google remains better at it than the competition," executive editor Cherlynn Low said. "If you don't have a big problem with AI features or find it easy to ignore or disable them, you'll find the Pixel 11 Pro to be arguably the best Android phone of its size and price."
Google Pixel 11
Despite minimal changes from the Pixel 10, and a $100 price increase, deputy news editor Nathan Ingraham argued the Pixel 11 is still the best Pixel phone for most people — even iPhone owners. "If you're coming from a Pixel older than last year's model, the Pixel 11 will represent a significant upgrade," he said. "And if you want to switch away from the iPhone for whatever reason, I can't think of a better first Android experience than what you'll get with the Pixel 11."
Google Pixel Watch 5
The Pixel Watch 5 is going to be a fantastic smartwatch... eventually. The wearable device is missing features right now, but Cherlynn explained that it still does just enough to justify the price increase. "As it stands, the Pixel Watch 5 is a very good smartwatch," she said. "At this point, I don't think any of the features I have yet to test are going to make the watch worse in some measurable way."
HP Omnibook X
If you're looking for a new Windows laptop, senior reviews writer Devindra Hardawar was impressed with HP's Omnibook X. According to him, it's only an SD card reader and better speakers away from near-perfection, mostly because the company paid attention to the essentials. "The Omnibook X is the perfect ultraportable for anyone who wants a capable and reliable machine without much flash," he said. "It's a reminder that simply getting the fundamentals right can make for a very compelling product."
Pebble Time 2
There's no denying the mass appeal of the original Pebble watch among gadget lovers. As you might expect, senior writer Daniel Cooper was relieved to see a device hit his desk (and wrist) that showed some restraint in the age of all AI everything. "The Pebble Time 2 is probably not for you, and that's fine, because it fulfills a vital role for those of us who crave something less from their watches," he said. "And, if I'm honest, even if the majority of people don't want one of these things, the tech ecosystem desperately needs it."
Alienware, GoPro, Pokémon and more
If all of those new gadgets aren't your cup of tea, we tackled other product categories over the last two weeks as well. Devindra put Alienware's 39-inch curved gaming display through its paces and Sam started his battle career in Pokémon Champions. In terms of cameras, contributing reviews writers James Trew and Steve Dent tested the GoPro Mission 1 Pro ILS and Panasonic Lumix L10, respectively. In more niche devices, Sam reviewed the Nimble SharePower and senior writer Mat Smith stayed cool with Sony's wearable air conditioner.

title_en: What You Should Look For In A USB To Bluetooth Adapter For PC
title_fa: What You Should Look For In A USB To Bluetooth Adapter For PC
excerpt_en: Not all adapters handle Bluetooth devices equally well. The right blend of speed, range, and reliability keeps your wireless gear working the way you expect.
excerpt_fa: Not all adapters handle Bluetooth devices equally well. The right blend of speed, range, and reliability keeps your wireless gear working the way you expect.
content_en:
What You Should Look For In A USB To Bluetooth Adapter For PC
The essentials behind a tiny but crucial upgrade.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
From keyboards to speakers, more and more parts of the PC experience are being brought to wireless form. Given the many conveniences afforded by wireless components, such as saving time on pulling and plugging wires or the added comfort afforded by that saved space, tech that doesn't integrate Bluetooth inherently could get left behind. Fortunately, Bluetooth adapters are a simple way to easily bridge this gap — though choosing the right option for the job is less than straightforward.
When deciding which Bluetooth adapter to invest in, USB options are as good a place to start as any. Not only is installation via a USB port often simpler than a direct implementation into the motherboard, as is the case with PCIe cards, USB ports are also more universal than PCIe slots. However, the best choice here still varies and will depend on what you're looking for — whether that's the quality of the connection, the number of devices you want to connect, capability for dual connectivity with both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, or simply budget.
How to choose a USB to Bluetooth adapter
Those who are simply looking to pair a headset with their PC can find serviceable USB Bluetooth adapters in the $10 range. Solid products at this price include the ASUS USB-BT500 or the TP-Link Nano 2-in-1 AC600. These options offer a quick start-up, and their compact design will save users from dealing with cheap, possibly flimsy antennae.
On the other hand, those looking for a more complex setup, with multiple devices or a high-quality connection, will want to dive into specs. When it comes to audio quality, you'll need to look into Bluetooth codecs — the different ways in which adapters translate sound via Bluetooth. While every Bluetooth device supports the standard SBC codec, options like the Avantree DG80 support AptX Low Latency, which offers a higher bitrate of 352 kbps (meaning higher audio quality overall). However, in terms of general low latency, the DG80 is audio-only. For more multi-purpose adapters, you'll want to pay attention to the available codecs, the latency stats, and whether the adapter is compatible with devices outside of audio. In this case, the Creative BT-W5 might prove the better option.
In terms of multi-device support, the Sena UD100-G03 is a solid example. This model supports up to seven simultaneous connections with a 900-foot range, which can be extended out to more than half a mile with upgrades. The capability to increase range, as well as the number of devices supported, are key factors when considering a device for this role.
What to check before buying any Bluetooth adapter
Before committing to any device, there are a few things you'll want to check first. This includes the different iterations of Bluetooth, with the current generation being 6.3. Fortunately, Bluetooth generations 5.0 and beyond are backwards-compatible with older devices, so you generally don't need to worry about which generation is which. Still, a quick check couldn't hurt.
The big things you'll want to keep track of include whether the adapter you want works for your device, as options like Noble's Sceptre are only USB-C, similar to the aforementioned Creative BT-W5. On that same track, you'll also need to make sure any given adapter works with your brand of PC, as well as whether it has all the capabilities you want (especially if you're using Bluetooth for more than just audio devices). Of course, it's wise to check whether your device of choice already has Bluetooth integration before spending any money on external hardware.

title_en: Nvidia’s AI advantage is moving beyond the GPU
title_fa: مزیت هوش مصنوعی انویدیا فراتر از GPU است
excerpt_en: The new generation of data center systems is increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles.
excerpt_fa: نسل جدید سیستم های مرکز داده با کنترل ترافیک هوشمندتر به جای چرخه های بیشتر پردازنده، کارایی را افزایش می دهد.
content_en:
Before this week, the dominant story about Nvidia went something like this: For the first few years of the AI boom, Nvidia was the only source for state-of-the-art GPUs, which became immensely profitable as the industry scaled out. In the last few years, hyperscalers like Amazon and Google have started building their own chips, and Nvidia is no longer the only game in town, leading many investors to wonder how durable its advantage really is.
It’s a compelling story, and mostly true. After growing its market cap 10x between the start of 2023 and mid-2025, Nvidia shares have been on a more modest trajectory for the past year, driven by concerns about GPU competition.
A new narrative has taken shape since the company’s earnings on Wednesday and investors are starting to realize that Nvidia’s advantage goes far beyond GPUs. As AI’s compute grows into the gigawatt scale, orchestration has become an increasingly complex task. Not surprisingly, Nvidia has built much of the state-of-the-art hardware needed to handle it, giving the company a huge advantage in the systems that surround the GPU even as it sees increased competition on the GPUs themselves.
For all the talk of compute as a commodity, it’s still incredibly difficult to operate a megascale data center at peak efficiency — and as deployments get bigger and faster, that challenge is only growing.
Rack by Rack
You can see some of this just by looking at the details of what Nvidia is actually selling. The company is currently rolling out its Vera Rubin architecture, which pairs the Rubin GPU with a collection of other units, including the Vera CPU, the Groq 3 LPX inference accelerator and similar racks for storage and networking.
Over the past week, I’ve been talking to folks at Nvidia about what those systems actually do, and the results have been surprising. Like the Rubin GPU itself, they’re extremely specialized systems, but instead of churning through tokens, they’re making sure everything outside the GPU works as efficiently as possible. If the GPU is the engine, these are the rest of the car.
The Vera CPU in particular is focused on the problem of orchestrating data. “Vera is important because there’s only so much memory that you can put in a single server or any sort of compute platform,” Jason Hardy, Nvidia’s VP of storage technology, told me.
As data centers have scaled up computing power, memory capacity has scaled up too, which is why companies like Micron have gotten rich in the second wave of the infrastructure boom. But getting that data to the GPU at the right time isn’t straightforward — and as companies look to drive tokens-per-watt lower and lower, they’re realizing how important that kind of traffic direction is.
“We saw upwards of 3x improvement in these operations, where the Vera CPU is allowing for acceleration,” Hardy said. “So now we can use our flash to its fullest potential, because we can get all that performance out of it without bottlenecking.”
You can see versions of the same problem outside of Nvidia. When OpenAI developed its Jalapeño chip, a major focus was avoiding these challenges entirely by minimizing the amount of data that needs to be moved around.
“We designed Jalapeño to minimize data movement and communication delays,” the company said in a blog post earlier this month. “Its large domain allows the entire workload to remain within one connected system, minimizing data movement and helping the complete request stay fast and efficient from beginning to end.”
It’s a different approach, avoiding data movement entirely by conducting a workload within one integrated chip. But the overall logic is the same, increasing efficiency with smarter traffic control instead of just more processor cycles. That in turn opens up a whole new layer of infrastructure for companies to compete over.
This new focus on data orchestration isn’t automatically a win for Nvidia. The company will have to compete with rival chipmakers and hyperscalers just as it has with GPUs. But the competition has moved to a new layer, where building a rival GPU matters less than being able to make the entire system work efficiently.
And at least in the early stages, Nvidia looks to have a commanding lead.
content_fa:
پیش از این هفته، داستان غالب در مورد انویدیا چیزی شبیه به این بود: در چند سال اول رونق هوش مصنوعی، انویدیا تنها منبع برای پردازنده‌های گرافیکی پیشرفته بود که با گسترش صنعت بسیار سودآور شد. در چند سال گذشته، هایپراسکیلرهایی مانند آمازون و گوگل شروع به ساخت تراشه های خود کرده اند، و انویدیا دیگر تنها بازی در شهر نیست، و بسیاری از سرمایه گذاران را وادار به تعجب کرده است که مزیت آن واقعا چقدر بادوام است.
این یک داستان متقاعد کننده است و بیشتر واقعی است. پس از افزایش 10 برابری ارزش بازار خود بین آغاز سال 2023 تا اواسط سال 2025، سهام انویدیا در سال گذشته در مسیر معتدل تری قرار داشته است که دلیل آن نگرانی ها در مورد رقابت پردازنده گرافیکی است.
روایت جدیدی از زمان درآمدهای این شرکت در روز چهارشنبه شکل گرفته است و سرمایه گذاران شروع به درک این موضوع کرده اند که مزیت انویدیا بسیار فراتر از پردازنده های گرافیکی است. همانطور که محاسبات هوش مصنوعی در مقیاس گیگاوات رشد می کند، ارکستراسیون به یک کار پیچیده تبدیل شده است. جای تعجب نیست که انویدیا بسیاری از سخت افزارهای پیشرفته مورد نیاز برای مدیریت آن را ساخته است و به این شرکت مزیت بزرگی را در سیستم هایی که GPU را احاطه کرده اند، می دهد، حتی با وجود افزایش رقابت در خود پردازنده های گرافیکی.
با وجود تمام صحبت‌هایی که در مورد محاسبات به عنوان یک کالا مطرح می‌شود، هنوز کارکردن یک مرکز داده در مقیاس بزرگ با حداکثر کارایی بسیار دشوار است – و با بزرگ‌تر و سریع‌تر شدن استقرار، این چالش تنها در حال رشد است.
رک با رک
شما می توانید برخی از این موارد را فقط با مشاهده جزئیات آنچه که Nvidia واقعاً می فروشد، مشاهده کنید. این شرکت در حال حاضر در حال ارائه معماری Vera Rubin خود است که GPU Rubin را با مجموعه‌ای از واحدهای دیگر، از جمله CPU Vera، شتاب‌دهنده استنتاج Groq 3 LPX و رک‌های مشابه برای ذخیره‌سازی و شبکه جفت می‌کند.
در هفته گذشته، من با افراد حاضر در انویدیا در مورد آنچه که این سیستم‌ها واقعاً انجام می‌دهند صحبت کرده‌ام و نتایج شگفت‌انگیز بوده است. مانند خود پردازنده‌های گرافیکی Rubin، آنها سیستم‌های بسیار تخصصی هستند، اما به‌جای اینکه از طریق توکن‌ها بچرخند، مطمئن می‌شوند که همه چیز خارج از GPU تا حد امکان کارآمد باشد. اگر پردازنده گرافیکی موتور است، اینها بقیه ماشین هستند.
CPU Vera به طور خاص بر مشکل هماهنگ سازی داده ها متمرکز است. جیسون هاردی، معاون فناوری ذخیره سازی انویدیا، به من گفت: «ورا مهم است زیرا فقط حافظه زیادی وجود دارد که می توانید آن را در یک سرور یا هر نوع پلت فرم محاسباتی قرار دهید.
همانطور که مراکز داده قدرت محاسباتی را افزایش داده اند، ظرفیت حافظه نیز افزایش یافته است، به همین دلیل است که شرکت هایی مانند Micron در موج دوم رونق زیرساخت ها ثروتمند شده اند. اما رساندن این داده‌ها به GPU در زمان مناسب کار ساده‌ای نیست – و از آنجایی که شرکت‌ها به دنبال کاهش و کاهش توکن‌ها در هر وات هستند، متوجه می‌شوند که این نوع جهت‌گیری ترافیک چقدر مهم است.
هاردی گفت: "ما شاهد بهبود 3 برابری در این عملیات بودیم، جایی که CPU Vera اجازه شتاب را می دهد." "بنابراین اکنون می توانیم از فلش خود تا حداکثر پتانسیل خود استفاده کنیم، زیرا می توانیم بدون ایجاد گلوگاه از آن همه عملکرد استفاده کنیم."
شما می توانید نسخه های مشابه مشکل را در خارج از Nvidia مشاهده کنید. هنگامی که OpenAI تراشه Jalapeño خود را توسعه داد، تمرکز اصلی بر اجتناب از این چالش‌ها با به حداقل رساندن حجم داده‌هایی بود که باید جابجا شوند.
این شرکت در یک پست وبلاگی در اوایل این ماه گفت: "ما Jalapeño را برای به حداقل رساندن تاخیرهای انتقال داده و ارتباطات طراحی کردیم." دامنه بزرگ آن به کل حجم کاری اجازه می دهد تا در یک سیستم متصل باقی بماند، حرکت داده ها را به حداقل می رساند و کمک می کند تا درخواست کامل از ابتدا تا انتها سریع و کارآمد بماند.
این یک رویکرد متفاوت است، با انجام یک بار کاری در یک تراشه یکپارچه، به طور کامل از جابجایی داده ها جلوگیری می کند. اما منطق کلی یکسان است، افزایش کارایی با کنترل ترافیک هوشمندتر به جای چرخه های بیشتر پردازنده. این به نوبه خود یک لایه کاملاً جدید از زیرساخت را برای رقابت شرکت ها باز می کند.
این تمرکز جدید بر روی هماهنگ‌سازی داده‌ها به‌طور خودکار یک پیروزی برای Nvidia نیست. این شرکت باید همانند پردازنده‌های گرافیکی با سازندگان تراشه‌های رقیب و هایپراسکیلرها رقابت کند. اما رقابت به لایه جدیدی منتقل شده است، جایی که ساخت یک GPU رقیب کمتر از توانایی کارآمد کردن کل سیستم اهمیت دارد.
و حداقل در مراحل اولیه، به نظر می‌رسد انویدیا پیشتاز بزرگی باشد.

title_fa: گلکسی زد فلیپ 8 در بهترین حالت خود وقتی اصطکاک وجود دارد

content_en:
What do you want from a flip phone when it’s closed? A simple interface, perhaps notifications and a widget or two, for handling the basics? Or a fully fledged Android experience shrunk down for the Flip form factor? For years, Samsung has insisted on the former, even as some fans — and Razr rival Motorola — have pushed for the latter. With the Galaxy Z Flip 8, Samsung has given in.
The Galaxy Z Flip 8 is at its best when there’s friction
The cover screen feels more like a phone than ever, but the limitations are still what makes it.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.
Although the Z Flip 8’s hardware is almost unchanged year-on-year, Samsung has fundamentally rethought how this phone is meant to be used when shut. The cover screen feels more like a regular Android phone, with easier access to the full versions of every single app, letting you browse social media, watch movies, and play games without ever opening the phone. Not every app works well on a tiny square screen with two cameras in the middle of it, but even when they don’t, that friction between me and the distractions of my phone still feels as much a feature as a bug.
The Good
- Runs any app on the cover screen
- Thinner and lighter
- Reliable battery
The Bad
- Mostly a rehash of last year’s phone
- Still vulnerable to dust
- $100 more expensive than the Z Flip 7
Everything exciting about the Z Flip 8 lies in its 4-inch cover screen, which is now more versatile than ever thanks to a homescreen redesign. Swiping down from the top left now brings up your notifications, while swiping from the top right instead shows a cover-screen-optimized version of the Quick Settings panel. Immediately, this feels more like a phone.
More exciting is what happens when you swipe up from the bottom: you get an app drawer. By default, this is populated with a selection of Samsung’s own apps that are optimized for the square screen, plus a “Labs” section with third-party options including Netflix and WhatsApp. But right below that, Samsung has included an easy prompt to install MultiStar, the Good Lock module that lets you run any app you’d like on the outer screen.
Samsung used to bury the option deep in the phone’s settings, only to be found by those who knew to look for it. The bottom of the app drawer isn’t quite front and center, but it’s much more prominent than it used to be.
You can still run apps in three forms: full-screen, with the cameras blocking part of the software; a square display that stops just above the level of the cameras; or a thin portrait-aspect ratio that letterboxes the sides. A small virtual button at the bottom of the screen lets you cycle through them.
Good performance isn’t guaranteed. Some apps, like Withings’ health tracker companion app, are almost impossible to use on the cover screen, with no configuration that leaves enough space for its graphs to fit. Google Maps is only a bit better — I love the idea of quickly checking my walking route without opening the phone, but there are so many floating interface elements that it’s unwieldy at best. Others work smoothly, but feel pointless: I can stream HBO Max on the tiny outer display, but I’d never want to.
But for other apps, the new cover screen options feel genuinely freeing. I can open Todoist and tick off a task, dip into WhatsApp to send a message, or open MyFitnessPal to log the snack I just ate. They’re quick actions that work well enough on the small screen, and because other apps — *cough* Instagram *cough* — don’t, I can dive into them without the risk of getting dragged into doomscrolling. That little bit of friction is just enough to save me from wasting 20 minutes I’ll never get back.
As for the hardware, little has changed. The Z Flip 8 is 0.6mm thinner and 8g lighter than its predecessor. This is the thickest of Samsung’s three current foldables, but it’s more compact than Motorola’s Razrs, its only real rivals.
Samsung didn’t upgrade the Z Flip 8 with the thinner, tougher titanium display stack found in the two new Z Fold 8 phones, which also means this has just as visible a crease as ever. It rarely bothers me, and is hard to see head-on, but you may feel differently. The IP48 rating is a more objective issue, and means that while this phone is mostly safe from water, it’s still vulnerable to dust.
On the inside, you’ll find the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 if you’re in the US, though my UK model runs Samsung’s Exynos 2600. Exynos chips get a bad rep, but performance has been smooth so far, and I have no real complaints.
As with the Z Fold 8 phones, Samsung switched to more energy-dense silicon-carbon batteries for the Z Flip 8. Unlike those phones, it didn’t actually increase the battery capacity, but instead used smaller cells with the same 4,300mAh capacity — the key to shrinking the phone itself. Still, battery life is solid, reliably lasting the full day with battery to spare. The charging — 25W wired, 15W wireless — is relatively unimpressive, and the only way to get Qi2 charging is still by using a compatible magnetic case.
Storage and RAM remain the same as on the Z Flip 7; the screens do too apart from small bumps to peak brightness, and the cameras are also identical to last year’s. The 50-megapixel main camera is impressive, and especially helpful since the form factor means you can use it for selfies too. The 12-megapixel ultrawide and 10-megapixel inner camera aren’t remarkable, but they get the job done. A slab phone at this price would have better cameras, and most likely a telephoto lens, but the lenses here are good enough.
The question is whether it’s all good enough for the price, given Samsung has bumped the Z Flip 8 up to $1,199.99, a $100 increase. Z Flip 7 owners certainly shouldn’t upgrade, and anyone else should consider buying that phone instead, since the difference between the two is slight.

وقتی گوشی تاشو بسته است از آن چه می خواهید؟ یک رابط کاربری ساده، شاید اعلان ها و یک یا دو ویجت، برای رسیدگی به اصول اولیه؟ یا تجربه کامل اندروید به دلیل فرم فاکتور Flip کاهش یافته است؟ سال‌ها، سامسونگ بر روی اولی پافشاری کرده است، حتی زمانی که برخی از طرفداران - و رقیب Razr موتورولا - برای دومی فشار آورده‌اند. سامسونگ با گلکسی زد فلیپ 8 تسلیم شد.
گلکسی زد فلیپ 8 در بهترین حالت خود وقتی اصطکاک وجود دارد
صفحه نمایش پوششی بیش از هر زمان دیگری شبیه یک گوشی است، اما محدودیت ها همچنان آن را ایجاد می کنند.
اگر چیزی را از پیوند Verge خریداری کنید، Vox Media ممکن است کمیسیون دریافت کند. بیانیه اخلاقی ما را ببینید.
اگرچه سخت افزار Z Flip 8 نسبت به سال گذشته تقریباً بدون تغییر است، سامسونگ اساساً در مورد نحوه استفاده از این تلفن در هنگام بسته شدن تجدید نظر کرده است. صفحه نمایش پوششی بیشتر شبیه یک گوشی اندرویدی معمولی است، با دسترسی آسان تر به نسخه های کامل هر برنامه، به شما امکان می دهد بدون باز کردن گوشی، رسانه های اجتماعی را مرور کنید، فیلم تماشا کنید و بازی کنید. همه برنامه‌ها روی یک صفحه‌نمایش مربع کوچک با دو دوربین در وسط آن به خوبی کار نمی‌کنند، اما حتی اگر این کار را نمی‌کنند، اصطکاک بین من و حواس‌پرتی‌های گوشی من همچنان به اندازه یک باگ یک ویژگی است.
خوب
- هر برنامه ای را روی صفحه نمایش اجرا می کند
- نازک تر و سبک تر
- باتری قابل اعتماد
بد
- عمدتاً بازنگری تلفن سال گذشته
- هنوز در برابر گرد و غبار آسیب پذیر است
- 100 دلار گرانتر از Z Flip 7
همه چیز هیجان انگیز در مورد Z Flip 8 در صفحه نمایش 4 اینچی آن نهفته است که اکنون به لطف طراحی مجدد صفحه اصلی همه کاره تر از همیشه شده است. کشیدن انگشت از بالا سمت چپ اکنون اعلان‌های شما را نشان می‌دهد، در حالی که کشیدن انگشت از بالا سمت راست به جای آن، یک نسخه بهینه‌شده برای صفحه‌نمایش پانل تنظیمات سریع را نشان می‌دهد. بلافاصله، این بیشتر شبیه یک تلفن است.
هیجان انگیزتر این است که وقتی از پایین به بالا بکشید اتفاق می افتد: یک کشوی برنامه دریافت می کنید. به‌طور پیش‌فرض، این مجموعه با مجموعه‌ای از برنامه‌های خود سامسونگ که برای صفحه‌نمایش مربعی بهینه شده‌اند، به‌علاوه یک بخش «آزمایشگاه‌ها» با گزینه‌های شخص ثالث از جمله Netflix و WhatsApp پر شده است. اما درست زیر آن، سامسونگ یک فرمان آسان برای نصب MultiStar، ماژول Good Lock که به شما امکان می‌دهد هر برنامه‌ای را که می‌خواهید بر روی صفحه بیرونی اجرا کنید، قرار داده است.
سامسونگ این گزینه را در اعماق تنظیمات گوشی دفن می‌کرد، اما کسانی که می‌دانستند آن را جستجو کنند پیدا می‌شود. پایین کشوی برنامه کاملاً جلو و وسط نیست، اما بسیار برجسته‌تر از قبل است.
همچنان می‌توانید برنامه‌ها را به سه شکل اجرا کنید: تمام صفحه، با مسدود کردن بخشی از نرم‌افزار توسط دوربین‌ها. یک صفحه نمایش مربعی که درست بالاتر از سطح دوربین ها متوقف می شود. یا یک نسبت پرتره به ابعاد نازک که کناره‌ها را در جعبه نامه قرار می‌دهد. یک دکمه مجازی کوچک در پایین صفحه به شما این امکان را می دهد که در آنها بچرخید.
عملکرد خوب تضمین نشده است. استفاده از برخی از برنامه‌ها، مانند برنامه همراه ردیاب سلامت Withings، تقریباً غیرممکن است، بدون پیکربندی که فضای کافی برای قرار گرفتن نمودارهای آن باقی می‌گذارد. Google Maps فقط کمی بهتر است - من عاشق این ایده هستم که مسیر پیاده روی خود را بدون باز کردن تلفن بررسی کنم، اما عناصر رابط شناور زیادی وجود دارد که در بهترین حالت سخت است. دیگران به آرامی کار می کنند، اما بی معنی هستند: من می توانم HBO Max را روی صفحه نمایش کوچک بیرونی پخش کنم، اما هرگز نمی خواهم.
اما برای سایر برنامه‌ها، گزینه‌های جدید صفحه روی جلد واقعاً آزاد هستند. می‌توانم Todoist را باز کنم و یک کار را علامت بزنم، برای ارسال پیام به واتس‌اپ وارد شوم، یا MyFitnessPal را باز کنم تا میان وعده‌ای را که تازه خورده‌ام ثبت کنم. آنها اقدامات سریعی هستند که به اندازه کافی روی صفحه نمایش کوچک کار می کنند، و از آنجایی که سایر برنامه ها - *سرفه* اینستاگرام *سرفه* - این کار را نمی کنند، می توانم بدون خطر کشیده شدن به Doomscrolling در آنها شیرجه بزنم. همین کمی اصطکاک کافی است تا من را از هدر دادن 20 دقیقه ای که هرگز برنمی گردم نجات دهد.
در مورد سخت افزار، کمی تغییر کرده است. Z Flip 8 0.6 میلی متر نازک تر و 8 گرم سبک تر از مدل قبلی خود است. این ضخیم‌ترین در بین سه تاشو فعلی سامسونگ است، اما از Razrs موتورولا، تنها رقیب واقعی آن، فشرده‌تر است.
سامسونگ Z Flip 8 را با صفحه نمایش تیتانیومی نازک‌تر و سخت‌تر که در دو گوشی جدید Z Fold 8 یافت می‌شود، ارتقا نداده است، این بدان معناست که این صفحه‌نمایش مانند همیشه چین‌خوردگی دارد. به ندرت من را آزار می دهد، و به سختی می توان آن را به طور مستقیم دید، اما ممکن است احساس متفاوتی داشته باشید. رده‌بندی IP48 موضوعی عینی‌تر است و به این معنی است که اگرچه این تلفن عمدتاً از آب در امان است، اما همچنان در برابر گرد و غبار آسیب‌پذیر است.
در داخل، اگر در ایالات متحده هستید، Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 را خواهید یافت، اگرچه مدل بریتانیایی من از Exynos 2600 سامسونگ استفاده می کند. تراشه های Exynos عملکرد بدی دارند، اما عملکرد تا کنون نرم بوده است و من هیچ شکایت واقعی ندارم.
همانند گوشی‌های Z Fold 8، سامسونگ برای Z Flip 8 به باتری‌های کربنی سیلیکونی با انرژی بیشتری روی آورد. برخلاف آن گوشی‌ها، در واقع ظرفیت باتری را افزایش نداد، بلکه در عوض از سلول‌های کوچک‌تر با همان ظرفیت 4300 میلی‌آمپر ساعت استفاده کرد - کلید کوچک کردن خود گوشی. با این حال، عمر باتری ثابت است و به طور قابل اعتمادی تمام روز را بدون باتری نگه می دارد. شارژ - 25 وات سیمی، 15 وات بی سیم - نسبتاً چشمگیر است و تنها راه برای شارژ Qi2 هنوز استفاده از یک قاب مغناطیسی سازگار است.
فضای ذخیره سازی و رم مانند Z Flip 7 باقی می ماند. صفحه نمایش ها جدا از برآمدگی های کوچک به حداکثر روشنایی می رسند و دوربین ها نیز مشابه سال گذشته هستند. دوربین اصلی 50 مگاپیکسلی چشمگیر است و به ویژه مفید است زیرا فاکتور فرم به این معنی است که می توانید از آن برای سلفی نیز استفاده کنید. دوربین داخلی 12 مگاپیکسلی فوق عریض و 10 مگاپیکسلی قابل توجه نیستند، اما کار را انجام می دهند. یک تلفن اسلب با این قیمت دوربین های بهتری دارد و به احتمال زیاد لنز تله فوتو دارد، اما لنزهای اینجا به اندازه کافی خوب هستند.
با توجه به اینکه سامسونگ Z Flip 8 را به 1199.99 دلار رسانده است، آیا همه اینها نسبت به قیمت مناسب هستند یا خیر. دارندگان Z Flip 7 مطمئناً نباید آن را ارتقا دهند و هر کس دیگری باید به جای آن گوشی را بخرد، زیرا تفاوت بین این دو ناچیز است.

title_en: How to use the new Siri app in iOS 27
title_fa: How to use the new Siri app in iOS 27
excerpt_en: How to use the new Siri app in iOS 27.
excerpt_fa: How to use the new Siri app in iOS 27.
content_en:
How to use the new Siri app in iOS 27
Assuming your device is new enough to use it.
Siri has been around since 2011, and for most of that time it's lagged behind assistants from Google, OpenAI and Anthropic. iOS 27 is Apple's attempt to close that gap, rebuilding the assistant with new AI capabilities and, for the first time, giving it a standalone app for conversational, chatbot-style use. Getting started with Siri AI on your iPhone is easy, as long as you meet a few requirements. This includes not only updating to iOS 27 first, but also checking to see if your device is compatible with Apple Intelligence.
Setting up Siri AI on iOS 27
Even if you have an iPhone running iOS 27, it may not be compatible with Siri AI. Apple Intelligence and the new Siri features are limited to the iPhone 15 Pro and later. Older iPhones, the base iPhone 15 included, are stuck with classic-and-dumb Siri.
You may also have some trouble using Siri AI depending on your region and language. For now, it only works in English. Users in the EU or China won't be able to access it either due to local regulations. Unfortunately, trying to change your iPhone's settings won't get around these restrictions.
After updating your iPhone to iOS 27, you'll be asked to enable Siri AI. If you chose not to at the time, you can still turn it on later by going to Settings > Siri and tap Turn On Siri. Then Try the new Siri. You may get instant access to Siri AI. However, some people land on a waitlist first. Beta testers have reported wait times anywhere from a few minutes to a few days.
Three ways to use Siri
The redesigned Siri can be reached three different ways. Swipe down from the Dynamic Island and a search box pops up. Holding down the side button still works if that's what you're used to. Maybe you want a more conventional chatbot experience like the one you get with ChatGPT? There's now a dedicated Siri app for that too.
The Siri app keeps a history of your past conversations synced via iCloud. It includes detailed responses with text cards, images and other media instead of just a simple reply. Want to give it more context? Tap the plus button to drop in an image or document. Or maybe you just want to ask "what's the weather forecast." All the classic commands work as usual.
Another great feature of the new Siri experience is how it has access to your personal context. Try asking about things like your messages or emails, and Siri will likely give you the answer you're expecting instead of just telling you to Google it.
Managing conversation history
There's a search button on the app's main screen if you're digging through old conversations. You can also flip between a list view and a card grid — just use the toggle in the upper-right corner. Want to pin one, rename it or get rid of it? Press and hold does the trick.
By default, iCloud keeps that history synced across every Apple device signed into the same account. To erase that history, Head to Settings > Siri > Keep Conversations. You get three options there: 30 days, one year or forever. Some short queries such as "set a timer" or "play a song" are not saved in Siri's history.
For now, iOS 27 is still in public beta, while the update typically releases in the fall. If you don't want to wait, the Beta Software Program is open to developers and testers. And remember to back up your iPhone, just in case the beta causes your favorite app to become buggy.

title_en: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters

content_en:
As audio-focused generative tools and platforms have gotten more sophisticated, the internet has become increasingly filled with AI-generated music whose melodies and vocals are algorithmically derived from the work of human artists. While some of the people pumping out this kind of content immediately own up to using AI, others have denied using the technology until increasing public scrutiny forced them to tell the truth.
Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
As AI infiltrates the electronic dance music scene, a callout culture is brewing.
For musicians — especially those creating art in technologically-focused spaces like electronic dance music — the increasingly complicated question of what is “real” and what isn’t feels particularly urgent and personal. Professional courtesy can make this only more complex; listeners can call out performers they suspect of using gen AI, but it’s something else for artists to raise concerns about their professional peers. There are some though, like 26-year-old EDM producer Max “H4RRIS” Harris, who are taking a stand against generative technology with videos calling out anyone they believe is trying to pass off AI slop as human-made art.
When I recently spoke with Harris, he told me that he sees AI-generated music as “a kind of decoy art form,” and he thinks that the people making it don’t really have anything meaningful to say with their creations. He feels that true art in any medium is “created by people that are trying to express feelings and messages,” and he believes that the only thing AI boosters are really interested in is making a quick profit.
“I don’t consider AI-generated material to be art, and I don’t think this technology is really advancing art in any meaningful way,” Harris said. “It’s a technological advancement that’s giving people a way to steal real art and pass it off as their own.”
Harris, originally from Maine, described his approach to making music as being fairly similar to working in other creative mediums. He always begins with a core concept before he starts “throwing more ideas down until I find something that sticks.” And as complicated as his workflow might look to someone unfamiliar with all of the tools and programs that he uses — his production setup includes Ableton Live, Novation Launchkey 49 MIDI controller, Ableton Push 3, Launchpad X, a couple of analog synthesizers, Serum, Diva, and the software sampler Kontakt — he said that the entire process is “really just me making creative decisions” that culminates in a sound that feels right.
“Each of those decisions — and there’s hundreds of them to go into each song — brings me closer to evoking a specific kind of idea or emotion,” Harris explained. “And then once I have a song mapped out, I have to start making even more choices about how to mix it in a way that makes it sound good and presentable.”
In Harris’ view, being a real artist means being able to make those kinds of experimental but informed creative decisions using your own studied understanding of a given medium. One of Harris’ biggest issues with gen AI is the way the technology often eliminates a user’s need to think about how songs (or books, films, podcasts, etc.) come together. But he has also been dismayed at the way that AI posers are muddying listeners’ understanding of what human-made EDM actually sounds like.
“Aside from the similar vocals, you can usually hear a sharp hissing throughout the track,” Harris said of AI-generated songs. “I think that comes from the way that these models often work by starting with a big white noise block and then making guesses about waveforms by referencing data taken from real songs.”
Harris pointed to MANSA’s “Midnight on My Mind” and Danny and Ian Asher’s “Take Me (To The Moon)” as what he thinks are examples of AI-produced songs that embody what he jokingly refers to as “the AI revolution” that’s responsible for polluting the EDM space. MANSA, Danny, and Asher have not publicly commented on whether they use generative tools in their music. But Harris and other EDM fans have noticed the similarities between “Take Me (To The Moon)” and another person’s AI-generated track. There’s no definitive evidence that MANSA produced “Midnight on My Mind” with AI. Harris could very well be wrong about these songs being generated with AI. But his insistence that they are reflects the larger culture of mistrust that has developed in response to the growing presence of AI content online.
“People are just straight up uploading original, copyrighted tracks of artists like Madonna and asking [AI] to remix them.”
Harris holds AI production company Suno responsible for the recent spike in this kind of music being uploaded to the internet, but he also credits specific quirks of the platform for helping him learn how to spot songs worth calling out.
“Something I’ve noticed with a lot of Suno-generated tracks is that a lot of the time, you’ll hear the vocals and other melodic elements will start stuttering at the same exact time,” Harris explained. “These models still have a hard time fully separating different parts of the songs they’re trained on, and they treat these elements like one big instrument. As a music producer, all of these things come across like choices that a human just wouldn’t make with their compositions because it just doesn’t make sense.”
In some instances, the visuals accompanying AI tracks are part of what prompts Harris to accuse people of slinging AI. You might not be able to hear the generative models behind evangelical Christian AI persona Lionsaddle’s music, but you can clearly see the character’s fingers vanishing in and out of existence in videos. There is also an overly glossy visual quality to most of the videos posted by Christian house musician Midnite Manna that makes their content look a lot like what we typically refer to as AI slop.

از آنجایی که ابزارها و پلتفرم‌های تولیدی متمرکز بر صدا پیچیده‌تر شده‌اند، اینترنت به طور فزاینده‌ای مملو از موسیقی تولید شده توسط هوش مصنوعی شده است که ملودی‌ها و آوازهای آن به‌طور الگوریتمی از کار هنرمندان انسانی مشتق شده‌اند. در حالی که برخی از افرادی که این نوع محتوا را تولید می کنند بلافاصله استفاده از هوش مصنوعی را به دست می آورند، برخی دیگر استفاده از این فناوری را انکار می کنند تا زمانی که بررسی های عمومی بیشتر آنها را مجبور به گفتن حقیقت کرد.
موزیسین‌هایی که به کارآگاه تبدیل شده‌اند، در حال شکار گرفترهای هوش مصنوعی هستند
با نفوذ هوش مصنوعی به صحنه موسیقی رقص الکترونیک، فرهنگ فراخوانی در حال شکل گیری است.
برای نوازندگان - به ویژه آنهایی که در فضاهای متمرکز بر فناوری مانند موسیقی رقص الکترونیکی هنر ایجاد می کنند - این سوال پیچیده تر از اینکه چه چیزی "واقعی" است و چه چیزی نیست، بسیار ضروری و شخصی است. حسن نیت حرفه ای می تواند این را پیچیده تر کند. شنوندگان می توانند مجریانی را که مشکوک به استفاده از هوش مصنوعی ژنرال هستند صدا بزنند، اما نگرانی هنرمندان در مورد همتایان حرفه ای خود چیز دیگری است. با این حال، برخی هستند، مانند مکس «H4RRIS» هریس، تهیه‌کننده 26 ساله EDM، که با ویدیوهایی که از هر کسی که فکر می‌کنند تلاش می‌کند تا شیطنت هوش مصنوعی را به‌عنوان هنر ساخته‌ی بشر جلوه می‌دهد، علیه فناوری مولد موضع بگیرد، موضع می‌گیرد.
وقتی اخیراً با هریس صحبت کردم، او به من گفت که موسیقی تولید شده توسط هوش مصنوعی را «نوعی شکل هنری فریبنده» می‌بیند، و فکر می‌کند که افرادی که آن را می‌سازند واقعاً چیزی برای گفتن با خلاقیت‌هایشان ندارند. او احساس می‌کند که هنر واقعی در هر رسانه‌ای «توسط افرادی ایجاد می‌شود که سعی در بیان احساسات و پیام‌ها دارند» و معتقد است که تنها چیزی که تقویت‌کنندگان هوش مصنوعی واقعاً به آن علاقه دارند، کسب سود سریع است.
هریس گفت: «من مواد تولید شده توسط هوش مصنوعی را هنر نمی‌دانم و فکر نمی‌کنم این فناوری واقعاً هنر را به‌طور معناداری پیش ببرد. "این یک پیشرفت تکنولوژیکی است که به مردم راهی می دهد تا هنر واقعی را بدزدند و آن را به عنوان متعلق به خود بگذرانند."
هریس که اصالتاً اهل مین است، رویکرد خود را در ساخت موسیقی تقریباً شبیه به کار در سایر رسانه‌های خلاق توصیف کرد. او همیشه قبل از اینکه شروع به "پرتاب ایده های بیشتر کند تا زمانی که چیزی را پیدا کنم که ثابت بماند" با یک مفهوم اصلی شروع می کند. و به همان اندازه که گردش کار او ممکن است برای کسی که با همه ابزارها و برنامه‌هایی که استفاده می‌کند ناآشنا به نظر برسد، پیچیده به نظر برسد - تنظیمات تولید او شامل Ableton Live، Novation Launchkey 49 MIDI controller، Ableton Push 3، Launchpad X، چند سینت سایزر آنالوگ، Serum، Diva و نرم‌افزاری است که به‌طور خلاقانه تصمیم‌گیری می‌کند. صدایی که حس درستی دارد

هریس در مورد آهنگ های تولید شده توسط هوش مصنوعی گفت: «به غیر از آوازهای مشابه، معمولاً می توانید صدای خش خش تند را در طول آهنگ بشنوید. من فکر می‌کنم این از روشی ناشی می‌شود که این مدل‌ها اغلب با شروع با یک بلوک نویز سفید بزرگ و سپس حدس زدن در مورد شکل موج با ارجاع داده‌های گرفته شده از آهنگ‌های واقعی، کار می‌کنند.»

You might not be able to hear the generative models behind evangelical Christian AI persona Lionsaddle’s music, but you can clearly see the character’s fingers vanishing in and out of existence in videos. There is also an overly glossy visual quality to most of the videos posted by Christian house musician Midnite Manna that makes their content look a lot like what we typically refer to as AI slop.
